Advertisement Advertisement The startups, Talentta and DAWN AI Study, emerged as winners of Meta’s AI Academy Startup Pitchathon at GITEX Nigeria, securing $5,000 each in equity-free funding and $2,000 in advertising credits to expand their platforms and reach more users. The two companies were selected from 10 finalists following more than 2,000 applications, highlighting growing interest among Nigerian entrepreneurs in building AI-powered solutions for local problems. Read also: Beyond film premieres, what Meta wants from Nollywood’s creator economy Talentta is developing an AI-powered career and workforce platform designed to connect young Nigerians with employment opportunities, particularly within their immediate communities. The platform helps users develop skills, assess their abilities, obtain certifications and identify available jobs. Its approach targets a persistent challenge in Nigeria’s labour market: the disconnect between people seeking employment and businesses looking for workers, particularly small and local enterprises that may not have the resources or reach to advertise vacancies through conventional recruitment channels. Advertisement Through an AI-powered WhatsApp agent, Talentta engages local businesses to identify their workforce requirements and connects them with potential employees. By using WhatsApp as an access point, the startup is seeking to reach job seekers and employers beyond traditional online recruitment platforms, where visibility, digital access and formal recruitment processes can limit participation. Advertisement The second winner, DAWN AI Study, is applying artificial intelligence to a different but equally significant challenge: the need for more personalised and inclusive learning experiences for children. The platform uses Meta’s Llama model to analyse speech and behavioural data, helping it understand individual learning needs and develop personalised learning pathways for school-age children. Advertisement Advertisement Its model is built around the recognition that children have different learning patterns and may require different approaches to understand and retain information. By using AI to identify these differences, DAWN AI Study aims to provide learning support that better accommodates individual needs. The startup’s approach also points to the potential application of AI beyond conventional educational tools, particularly in supporting children whose learning requirements may not be adequately addressed by standard classroom approaches. The emergence of both startups reflects a broader shift in Nigeria’s technology ecosystem, where entrepreneurs are exploring practical applications of AI in sectors with significant development challenges. While much of the global AI conversation has centred on productivity, automation and the development of increasingly sophisticated models, Talentta and DAWN AI Study are focusing on how the technology can improve access to employment opportunities and educational support. For Meta, the funding forms part of its efforts to support African entrepreneurs developing AI-powered products and services. “AI’s value will be judged by the real impact it has on people’s lives. Across our region, people are building solutions around the languages they speak, the businesses they run and the challenges their communities face. The Impact Grant and Hub are about giving more builders the support, skills and resources to turn those ideas into useful products and services. We want people here to help shape AI’s future, not simply use what others have built,” said Kojo Boakye, vice president of Public Policy for Africa, the Middle East and Türkiye at Meta. The financial support and advertising credits are expected to help the startups strengthen their products, increase visibility and expand their reach. However, the longer-term significance of the initiatives will depend on their ability to move beyond early-stage innovation and demonstrate measurable outcomes, including the number of job seekers connected to employment, businesses reached, children supported and improvements in learning experiences. Read also: Meta’s $95bn equity raise draws chipmakers as AI race drives spending For Talentta, the challenge will be converting connections between employers and job seekers into sustainable employment outcomes, particularly in a labour market where the availability of decent jobs remains a major concern. For DAWN AI Study, its ability to demonstrate that AI-driven personalisation translates into improved learning outcomes will be central to establishing the platform’s value to children, parents and educators. Their selection by Meta also underscores the growing importance of locally developed AI applications in determining how emerging technologies address Africa’s development priorities.
